raw_brief: Build a landing page for Haven, a secrets vault. Light.

surface.scope: single standalone page, offline-renderable from file://

product.name: Haven
product.category: secrets vault — credential and secret management for engineering teams
product.working_definition: Haven stores API keys, database credentials, certificates, and environment variables encrypted at rest, hands them out to people and services on request through short-lived, scoped grants instead of standing plaintext access, and logs every read so a team can answer 'who touched this secret, and when' without guessing.
product.rationale: The brief names only 'a secrets vault' with no further spec. A landing page cannot be built around an empty abstraction, so the director (this arm) fixed one concrete, plausible product identity consistent with the category (secret/credential management, the space HashiCorp Vault / Doppler / 1Password Secrets occupy) and held it fixed for every section. This is a creative decision, not a brief requirement — recorded here so it reads as intentional, not guessed mid-build.

audience.primary: engineers, SREs, and security leads at small-to-mid engineering orgs who currently pass secrets through .env files, Slack messages, or a shared password doc
audience.mindset_on_arrival: wary of another dashboard to babysit; wants to see exactly what changes about their daily workflow (request a secret, get a scoped grant, rotate) before trusting a vendor with credentials

outcome.primary_action: start a vault (primary CTA: get started / create a vault)
outcome.secondary_action: see how access works (secondary CTA + concrete product specimen: a real secret record and an access-log entry)
outcome.page_job: in one scroll, show what goes into Haven, how a person or service gets a secret out of it (a scoped, time-boxed grant, not a shared password), and what it refuses to do (no standing plaintext access, no silent reads) — enough for a wary engineer to trust the mechanism before creating an account

taste_profile.layout: mid-high — mostly grid-aligned with deliberate breaks (asymmetric hero, offset principle band); editorial enough for a marketing surface but never loose, because a vault's layout should read as precise, not playful
taste_profile.typography: mid-high — a considered modular scale with real weight contrast; restrained compared to a flashier consumer brand, because a security product's type should read calm and exact, not loud
taste_profile.spacing: mid — comfortable gallery rhythm in marketing bands, tight/dense inside the secret-record and access-log specimens (density argues 'the product is precise even where the marketing is spacious')
taste_profile.motion: mid — standard entrance and hover feedback only; deliberately not expressive/orchestrated, because a security surface earning trust should feel steady, not showy
taste_profile.iconography: mid — one consistent hand-authored line-icon set, single stroke weight, used for lock/key/grant/audit concepts
taste_profile.depth: low-mid — mostly flat with hairline borders; shadow reserved for exactly one raised state (the unlocked secret card) so elevation still means something
taste_profile.consistency: not scorable — first generation in an empty project workspace (spec 019 benchmark build), no established design system to inherit

mode.brand_accent: deep forest/pine green (~160-165° hue) as the signal color against a warm off-white paper background — chosen specifically outside the indigo/violet 'AI-glow' band per taste-rubric Axis 6 anti-pattern, and away from the generic security-product blue

constraints.offline: no CDN, no remote fonts, no remote images, no network requests — inline SVG / CSS / data URIs only, system font stack
constraints.effort: a complete, real landing page — genuine effort, not a stub
constraints.blinding: index.html must contain no comment, meta tag, footer credit, class name, or copy naming any model, vendor, tool, generator, 'DESIGN:OS', or 'AI'

out_of_scope: working backend, auth, or a live vault (CTAs are static anchors; the secret record and access log shown are labelled specimens)
fabricated customer logos, testimonials, or metrics (per page-structures.md §3 honest copy)
